newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks push higher at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks push higher at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks knocked down key resistance levels and closed higher on Monday despite a drop in volume attributed to the U.S. Presidents Day holiday, dealers said.
"Volume was stronger than we expected, underscoring the climate of optimism which prevails in the market," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index pierced the 730 mark and closed up 1.2 percent at 734.19, its highest level since June, 1992. The bolsa had capped an upward march at 728 exactly three years ago.
Traders said the market was absorbing profit-taking thanks to buying by the local pension funds, which snapped up positions shed by foreign institutional players.
Floor volume fell to 20.3 million pesos from 36.9 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover picked up to 116.4 million pesos from 191.2 million Friday.
The broad market index closed up 0.8 percent, with winners beating losers 33 to 12 and 20 stocks closing unchanged.
Top main-tier gaines were in Banco de Galicia, petrochemical concern Indupa and steelmaker Acindar, which ralled 2.7 percent, 2.6 percent and 2.5 percent, respectively.
The only MerVal losers were carmaker Sevel and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which fell 0.8 percent and 0.7 percent, respectively.
